title: Customer Identity Authority v1 — common types (CANDIDATE, CIA-S0)
description: Shared definitions of the CIA v1 consumer API. Channel names, channel subject formats, account namespaces and data purposes are values registered in configuration, never types of the core: the schemas only fix their lexical shape.

context.description: Omnichannel context asserted by the consumer's channel integration from an authenticated channel event (never by a model). The consumer itself is NOT in the body: it is the principal authenticated by the bearer.

channelAccountRef.description: The consumer's own account on the channel (configuration allowlist).

subjectRef.description: Channel subject as authenticated by the channel provider. Its exact format is registered per channel; the CIA stores only its keyed hash.

sessionRef.description: Opaque session/conversation reference of the consumer. Must be identical between starting and confirming a verification.

subjectAssurance.description: How the subject was authenticated. v1 accepts only a provider-signed event.

dataPurpose.description: Registered data-access purpose (configuration allowlist per consumer).

verificationPurpose.description: Why the verification is performed. Distinct from data-access purposes, which only grants carry.

accountRef.description: Commercial account reference with the namespace of a registered account provider: <namespace>:<id>.

verificationId.description: 128 random bits, base64url without padding. Kept by the channel integration; never shown to a model.

email.description: Declared by the user: untrusted. Characters that alter account-provider filters are rejected.

code.description: One-time code exactly as normalized by the channel integration.

grant.description: Per-customer access grant. token is a compact JWS (grant.v1.schema.json); consumers treat it as opaque.

expiresAt.description: Equals the exp claim of the token.

purposes.description: Equals the requested purposes; all must be granted.
